bucket_note: Seattle (SDOT) is A: open, licensed, GPS + street names + person KABCO. Statewide WSDOT is A*: record-level JSON with GPS and KABCO from an undocumented public portal endpoint, no licence, no street names. The full export (street names, offsets, vehicles) comes by free emailed request (Form 780-032), so statewide-with-names is D (bring your own export), with its reader built.

methods.rates_unit: none: WSDOT 'no longer uses crash rates for decision-making' (Safety Analysis Guide 2024, printed p.19); only statewide fatality and serious-injury rates per 100 million VMT for federal targets

crash_costs.year: not stated (applied to 2023 crashes; HSIP Implementation Plan 2024, Exhibit 6 note 3, printed p.11)

methods.screening_method: HSM SPFs + Empirical Bayes expected fatal + serious crash frequency, sliding window + peak searching; cut-off 0.5 expected (CAL/CAC) or 0.3 excess (IAL) crashes per year; calibration factor 1.00; 5 full calendar years (min 2)
differences_from_ca: No average crash-rate table (CA: TASAS base rates by rate group)
K and A priced the same ($4,308,200), no location-type split (CA LRSM 2026: KA by signalized / non-signalized / roadway)
Screening by SPF + EB excess; no hot spots or heat maps (CA tools rank by counts, rates, cost)
City Safety needs a Local Road Safety Plan and the KSI crash report numbers 2020-2024
Roundabout-first ICE with separate vehicle and active-transportation safety assessments
§148/§407 footer on every page, table or graph of safety analysis
CMFs from the WSDOT short list first; Clearinghouse needs approval (CA: LRSM Appendix B CRFs)
